To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the concentrations of inorganic and organic N and P were determined at monthly interval over a year from a peaty upland soil in northern England, that the organic forms dominated P, that there were pulses of organic P in the soil and streams, and that seasonal changes in the N:P ratio suggested that the availability of these nutrients may influence organisms.
organic forms of N and P were found in high concentrations and that the seasonal availability of N and P was likely to influence the biology of the streams.

1) organic N and P in upland soils are important sources of nutrients to organisms; 2) organic P is a major form of phosphorus in soil solution and streams; and 3) seasonal variation in N:P ratios suggests that some organisms may become nutrient-limited during spring, when the N:P ratio is lowest.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of organic nutrients in the ecology of upland streams and soils.
the role of organic nutrients in controlling the ecology of upland streams.
the availability of nitrogen ( N) and phosphorus( P) to organisms, and how this influences the ecology of upland ecosystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the availability of N and P to organisms is likely to be influenced by organic compounds, and that the seasonal dynamics of these organic nutrients are important for the ecology of upland streams.
the availability of organic P is a major control on the ecology and biodiversity of upland streams, but the availability of inorganic P and N also plays an important role.
inorganic N is the main source of N in the drainage streams, whereas organic P is the main source in both the soil solution and the streams.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
organic forms of P are the most abundant, and are likely to influence the availability of both P and N in upland waters.
organic N and P are important, and that their availability may change with season, but that the role of organic P is likely to be more significant.
organic N and organic P are important components of N and P cycles, but the relative significance of each is dependent upon the biological context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organic compounds of N and P can be important to the ecology of upland streams.
the presence of organic compounds in streams and soils can have a significant influence on the nutrient status of an ecosystem.
organic N and P are important for understanding the nutrient limitation of upland streams.
